text: The night was soft. The gum trees swayed and sighed.
Sunny watched the treetops, dark against the sky.
Then — whoosh! — a tiny shape leapt out and glided,
arms spread wide, across the starry night.
A little sugar glider, soft and grey,
with big dark eyes and a long and fluffy tail.
It landed on a branch not far away
and looked at Sunny with a friendly gaze.
“Hello!” it squeaked. “Did you see me fly?
I glide from tree to tree beneath the moon.”
It spread the soft skin between its little legs
and leapt again — a gentle, floating leap.
Sunny watched it sail from tree to tree,
silent as a leaf upon the evening breeze.
“You fly so soft,” said Sunny with a smile.
“Not fly,” it laughed. “I glide. Come rest a while.”
They sat together in the cosy dark
and watched the fireflies blink among the leaves.
The sugar glider yawned and curled its tail.
“It's time for me to sleep now,” it said soft.
It climbed into a hollow, warm and small,
and tucked its fluffy tail around its nose.
Sunny found a bed of moss below
and nestled down beneath the whispering tree.
Her eyes grew heavy in the gentle glow.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beneath the gliding stars,
as soft and safe as any sleeping thing.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little glider.
Goodnight, sleepy bush. Goodnight, little one.
